TONG CHUN I (童春意).
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [签名]

With reference to the attached file on the above
subject, I have to report that efforts made by the Chinese
detectives attached to Section 2 have as yet failed to establish
the identity of the suspect Tong Chun I (童春意), which name,
it is believed, to be an alias of Giau Tek Hum (饒狄云),
a prominent member of the Malayan Communist Party.
Chok Siew Chok (鄒兆作) alias Tseu Zao Tsoh
(兆作), the communication agent mentioned in H.B.M.
Consulate letter of June 12, 1935, is still employed in the
Current Account Department of the Kok Hoa Bank (國華銀行),
better known as the China State Bank, No.356 Peking Road, and
continuous to reside with his wife and family at No.13, Lane
233, Markham Road. A general observation has been kept on
his movements but nothing of a suspicious nature discovered.
The local Government Censors who were requested
sometime ago to intercept mail addressed to Chow Siew Chok,
and to pass same over to the Municipal Police for examination,
have so far been unable to furnish any useful information.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

Date August 6, 1935.
Subject Letter from H.B.M. Consulate-General re communist suspect TONG CHUN I
( 童春志 )。
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by D.S.I. Byrne

With reference to the address -- "Tong Chun I, c/o Mr.
Choh Siew Chok ( 鄒兆作 ), Kok Hoa Bank ( 國華 ), Shanghai" --
which is reported to be in use by certain members of the Malayan
Communist Party, I have to report that enquiries made have so
far been without result.
Tong Chun I is believed to be an alias used by a well-
known member of the Malayan Communist Party named Giau Tek Hun
( 饒狄雲 ) in order to cloak his identity. Although this
communication address has been in the possession of the Municipal
Police since July 1934, no concrete evidence has yet been
obtained to warrant any action. The characters of the name
of the communication agent Chok Siew Chok are identical with
those in the Tseu Zao Tsoh ( 鄒兆作 ), who was often mentioned
in previous reports. The latter is still in the employ of
the Deposit Department of the Kok Hoa Bank ( 國華 ) which is
better known as the China State Bank, No.356 Peking Road, and
is staying with his wife and family in a downstairs room of
house No.13, Lane 233, Markham Road. Tseu was recently kept
under observation by Chinese detectives attached to this
Section, but his movements revealed nothing.
Another communication address of Tong Chun I, known to
the Municipal Police, is the Shanghai Bookstore, No.8, Lane 36,
North Honan Road, whose head office is in Singapore. This shop
occupies the ground portion of that address and employs five
assistants, all of whom are natives of Ningpo. None of these
resides in the French Concession or is known to be friendly
with persons residing in Avenue Dubail.

Subject (in full) Letter dated July 16, 1934, from H.B.M. Consulate-General
re communist suspects Tong Chun I (童春意) et al.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [Signature] A/.

Exhaustive enquiries made concerning two communist
suspects named Tseu Zao Tsok(鄒兆作) and Giau Tek Hun(饒狄云)
elicit the information that latter is believed to assume the
alias of Tong Chun I (童春意) in order to cloak his identity.
Tseu Zao Tsok, an employee in the Deposit Department
of the China State Bank, 356 Peking Road, who is suspected of
having received mail matter on behalf of Giau Tek Hun, member
of the Malayan Communist Party, is at present living with his
wife and family in the home of his friend named Nying Tsoh Jung
(任卓群), age about 32, native of Wusieh, employee of the
branch office of the "Bank of Kiangsu" in that city, at No.20
Si Tek Li "步德里"(Lane 233) Markham Road. They occupy the
ground portion of the premises. The reason for Tseu's removal
from his former address - No.4, Lane 233, Markham Road - is
attributable to a reduction of the monthly allowance granted
by his elder brother who is a prominent shareholder of the China
State Bank and who is also connected with several other local
Chinese banks.

A general watch kept on the movements of Tseu Zao Tsok,
his possible visitors as well as mail matter received by him has
so far failed to disclose anything of a suspicious nature. Very
few letters addressed to him have been observed and these
generally appear to be of a friendly nature and usually emanate
from his relatives in Kwangtung and Hongkong.

House No.4, Lane 233, Markham Road, which was formerly
occupied by Tseu has been rented by one named Mao(茅), an
employee of the Dah Chong(大昌) Dispensary, Foochow Road,
since August 1, 1934.

Further discreet enquiries made in the neighbourhood

对名为邹兆作 (Tseu Zao Tsok)(鄒兆作) 和饶狄云 (Giau Tek Hun)(饒狄云) 的两名共产主义嫌疑分子进行的详尽调查，获得了如下信息：据信后者为了掩盖身份，使用了童春意 (Tong Chun I) (童春意) 这一化名。
邹兆作 (Tseu Zao Tsok) 是北京路356号中国国家银行储蓄部的职员，涉嫌代表马来亚共产党成员饶狄云 (Giau Tek Hun) 接收邮件，目前与其妻室家属居住在朋友任卓群 (Nying Tsoh Jung) (任卓群) 家中。任卓群，约32岁，吴县人，系江苏银行 (Bank of Kiangsu) 在该市分行的职员，住址为马克姆路 (Markham Road) “步德里” (Si Tek Li) (Lane 233) 20号。他们占用该房屋的地面部分。邹氏从原址——马克姆路 (Markham Road) 233弄4号——搬离的原因，归咎于其兄长减少了他每月的津贴。其兄长是中国国家银行的重要股东，并与当地其他几家华资银行有关联。

对邹兆作 (Tseu Zao Tsok) 的行动、可能的访客以及他收到的邮件进行的常规监视，迄今未发现任何可疑情况。观察到他收到的信件很少，且通常看似友好往来，一般来自他在广东和香港的亲属。

邹氏以前居住的马克姆路 (Markham Road) 233弄4号房屋，自1934年8月1日起已由一名姓茅 (Mao)(茅) 的人租用，茅某是福州路大昌 (Dah Chong)(大昌) 药房的职员。

Discreet enquiries made by C.D.C.281 regarding a certain
Chinese communist suspect named Tong Chun I (童春意) who is using
the following accomodation addresses (1) No.4, Bek Si Tek Li,
Shanghai (上海麦根路世德里四号 ) and (2) c/o Shanghai Book Store,
Hong Fook Li, Tien Hau Kong Bridge, North Honan Road, Shanghai
(上海北河南路天后宫桥洪福里上海书局中庄转 ), elicit the following :
Address (1) is situate at No.S-4, Lane 233, Markham
Road and is occupied by Tseu Zao Tsoh (邹肇作), an employee of
the China State Bank, 356 Peking Road. There are no other
families residing at this address. It will be recalled that
in a previous enquiry from H.B.M. Consulate-General, Tseu is
suspected of having received mail matter on behalf of a well-
known member of the Malayan Communist Party named Giau Tek Hun
(饶狄云) (vide file D-5589).
Address (2) is located at No.8, Lane 36, North Honan
Road. It is the local agency of the Shanghai Bookstore in
Singapore and was established in 1932. There are five people
employed in this establishment. Confidential enquiries disclose
that the name Tong Chun I is unknown at this address.
It is therefore surmised that the name Tong Chun I
is an assumed name used by Giau Tek Hun particulars of whom
have already been reported.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

Copy of Intercepted letter
Friends, Ban, He, Su and Hiap (漫, 霞, 樹, 俠)
Since I left Singapore I have now come to Shanghai, I have already sent you a letter and I think you must have received it. I am sorry that I have to leave in such a hurry and was unable to inform any of you but I think all of you will excuse me.
The coming New Year Holidays remind me of your activities of next year. But why should we be worried or frightened if we can help each other as we have done in the past. At present the only thing which I wish to know is your activities of next year, so please let me know in your reply.
Has He's family returned home ? How about Su's lover ? I have received two letters from Ban of the 9th and 12the Sept. and from which I know that all of you remember of me very much. That sum of money which you have sent me is indeed a great help to me. I know that the money has been sent to Mr Bun Thai (敏泰) as he had already informed me and he is going to remit it to me very soon.
How is the health of He, is he alright now ? Has Ban gone to Singapore and on what occasion does he go? It is a pity that I could not see him but circumstances have made it so. What can we do.
Our newspaper businesses have already started but unfortunately we were forced to stop it for some time. We are now going to carry on with the business again. We have decided to publish daily papers and after everything is settled we will publish other periodicals.
My address is (Yen Zao Yoh)
Giau Tek Hun (饒狄雲)
C/o Chiau Tiau Ghok (非作)
C/o Kok Hoa Bank,
Shanghai.
Ngan Dih Yun Yours,
Tek (狄 )
25.11.33
page_data.zh:
截获信件副本
朋友们，Ban, He, Su 和 Hiap (漫, 霞, 樹, 俠)
自从我离开新加坡后，现已来到上海，我已经给你们寄了一封信，我想你们一定收到了。很抱歉我不得不如此匆忙地离开，未能通知你们任何人，但我想你们都会原谅我。
即将到来的新年假期让我想起你们明年的活动。但是，如果我们能像过去那样互相帮助，又何必担忧或恐惧呢？目前我唯一想知道的是你们明年的活动，所以请在回信中告知我。
He 的家人回家了吗？Su 的爱人怎么样？我收到了 Ban 9日和12日的两封信，从中得知你们都非常想念我。你们寄给我的那笔钱确实对我帮助很大。我知道钱已经寄给了 Bun Thai (敏泰) 先生，因为他已经通知了我，他很快就会汇款给我。
